evals.name: generate-python-course
evals.prompt: Hey, my friend sent me this markdown Python tutorial at /tmp/eval-python-tutorial.md. Can you turn it into a hands-on course I can actually work through? I want real exercises with stub files I have to fill in, not just reading. Python. Put the course in ./python-tutorial-course/.
evals.expected_output: A directory ./python-tutorial-course/ containing _TEACHER.md, _meta.json, README.md, and at least 3 chapter directories (one per chapter in the source). Each lesson has exercises/, tests/, .solutions/ subdirs with .py files. Starter files contain '# TODO:' markers and header comments.

evals.name: generate-js-from-library-docs
evals.prompt: I concatenated the docs for a small JavaScript array helper library into /tmp/eval-js-docs.md. Make me a hands-on course — I learn by writing code, not reading. JavaScript. Output to ./array-course/.
evals.expected_output: A ./array-course/ directory with the same shape as eval 1, but .js files. _meta.json should have language=javascript and test_command=node.

evals.name: teach-mode-start-lesson
evals.prompt: I'm in /tmp/eval-existing-course/. Walk me through lesson 1. I want to understand what I'm learning, then I'll write the code.
evals.expected_output: A teacher-response.md transcript that: (a) reads _TEACHER.md and _meta.json, (b) presents a concise (3-5 bullet) summary of lesson 1, (c) points at the first exercise file path, (d) does NOT paste solution code, (e) does NOT auto-write code into the exercise file.
